page: Amazon Web Services c7i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes dedicated CPU allocation with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, which provides a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and specialized instruction performance. The Passmark CPU score, extended instructions test, encryption test, and physics test all rank in the top 25 percent. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks fall into the top 25 percent, while single-core performance in both stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the middle 50 percent. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, which contribute to strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing for small and medium models, as well as text generation for small models.

From a resource density perspective, the c7i.16xlarge offers high compute density with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core, making it cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network storage, which is a tradeoff for I/O-intensive tasks. However, the instance demonstrates strong performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, ranking in the top 25 percent. This supports workloads such as software compilation, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, but offers a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks indicate strong performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, cryptography, and database operations, placing it in the top 25 percent. It also performs well in LLM inference for small and medium models due to built-in AMX and AVX-512 instruction support. This instance is appropriate for compute-intensive workloads, including web serving, software compilation, and database management, where high CPU density is prioritized over large memory allocations.
